critical_code_review_comments: server.py still ~930 lines with all routes + auth + storage helpers — approaching maintainability threshold, consider splitting into routers/*.py (products, orders, seller, admin, payments, auth).

GET /api/products has no pagination or filters server-side; the whole catalog (33 seed + all approved seller products) is returned in one response. For scale, add ?category=, ?q=, ?limit=/?offset= server-side.
GET /api/products/{id} does an in-memory linear scan over _all_products(); fine at 33 rows but wasteful — query MongoDB directly by id in both collections.

ProductsContext refresh() swallows all errors silently and just sets [] on failure — a fetch failure will look identical to an empty catalog in the UI. Consider exposing an error state so the UI can show a real error banner instead of the empty state.

Seed on startup uses $setOnInsert (idempotent) but that means if BASE_PRODUCTS is edited later (e.g. price change on p-001), the existing DB doc will NOT be updated. Consider a versioned/full-upsert seed if catalog edits are expected.
No brute-force / rate limit on /api/auth/login (unchanged from iteration_2) — password guessing is unrestricted.
